page: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 128 dedicated vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per physical core. It does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results position this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 138,364.71 and a PassMark CPU score of 122,858.65. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only small block cached bandwidth of 10,222.53 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth of 392.84 GB/sec. It demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptographic operations, database processing, and Redis SET operations. Additionally, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions enable top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for compute-intensive workloads, software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 256.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, though it lacks local storage. The architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. In benchmarks, the instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and strong database processing capabilities, achieving 222.4 million Redis SET operations per second. It is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
